claims: The Artemis II mission is scheduled to splash down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California.
The Artemis II mission is scheduled to splash down on Friday, April 10, 2026.
The Artemis II mission is scheduled to splash down at approximately 8:07 p.m. EDT.
The Artemis II landing time is estimated at 8:07 p.m. EDT / 5:07 p.m. PDT on April 10, 2026.
The Orion spacecraft will re-enter Earth’s atmosphere at roughly 24,000 mph.
The Artemis II mission is a 10-day lunar flyby mission.
U.S. Navy and NASA personnel will secure the capsule and retrieve the crew.
The capsule will experience a roughly 6-minute communication blackout due to plasma buildup during re-entry.
Parachutes will deploy in stages to slow the capsule to roughly 20 mph for splashdown.
The Artemis II crew consists of Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
The Artemis II crew will be extracted by helicopter and taken to a Navy vessel.
The Artemis II mission is designed to test critical systems for future Artemis moon landings.
